logicalQualifications.finding: Third-figure moods1–2 require an existing M; fourth-figure mood1 requires an existing C, and mood4 an existing M. These conditions are noted rather than omitted under modern empty-class semantics.
The assumed D comes from the witness asserted by a particular premise, making its nonemptiness explicit.

The author’s conversion to four particular negative conditionals is retained. It cannot be identified without additional semantic and circumstance conditions with merely negating modern Boolean exclusive-or. The 1968 p269 confirms the wording, not validity under another semantics.
The author states conditions only for the two varieties sharing in the consequent, despite first outlining four varieties. The limitation is preserved.
The omitted external premise supplies transitivity. No blanket transitivity of all resemblance relations is added.

Biological, medicinal, fruit, and geometrical examples remain authorial examples. The ordinary-condition qualification, complete-similarity assumption, and possibility of revising a mistaken causal attribution are preserved.
School attribution is explicit. Certainty requires knowledge of the complete cause; merely shared properties do not suffice. The abbreviated legal report is not independently collated.
The exercise is retained with its “only” wording and without reversing implication to make the proposed inference valid.

review.method: All base prose/formula/exercise blocks read in consecutive bounded batches; English checked against the corresponding Arabic while drafted, with a final pass over negations, proof directions, conditional nesting, school attribution, and source qualifications.
